mainTopic: Wool of a holy animal: the expert requirement, the dispute of עקביא and the חכמים, the הלכה like רבי יהודה, and רבי ינאי's question about an עולה
overview: This amud is about the wool of a בכור (a firstborn animal). It first defends the view that a blemished בכור's wool is permitted only once a מומחה (expert) has officially permitted the blemish. The answer is that a ברייתא calls an animal 'תם' until an expert permits it. Next the גמרא quotes a ברייתא where עקביא בן מהללאל and the חכמים argue about the wool, and רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי each describe the dispute differently. The גמרא suggests that רבי יוסי and the תנא קמא differ over the expert requirement, but רבא rejects this. רבא explains that everyone requires an expert, and that the three תנאים disagree about which case is in dispute: an animal that died or one that was slaughtered. רב נחמן rules like רבי יהודה, based on a משנה in עדיות. רב נחמן בר יצחק supports this from the rule in our משנה about dangling wool. Finally, רבי ינאי asks about wool that fell out by itself from an unblemished עולה. The גמרא explains why a חטאת, an אשם, a בכור and a מעשר are clear cases, and the reasoning about the עולה continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Challenge: the blemished animal's wool seems permitted without an expert
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא draws an inference from the ברייתא: only a תם is forbidden, so a בעל מום would be permitted even without a מומחה. That contradicts the earlier view.
steps.simpleTranslation: But this implies that a blemished animal is permitted, even though no expert permitted it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is attacking the earlier view that a מומחה must permit the blemish. It points to a ברייתא that seems to permit the wool of any blemished animal, with or without an expert.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא forbade wool only from a בכור תם (an unblemished firstborn). By implication (the word הָא), a בכור בעל מום would be permitted. The ברייתא says nothing about an expert, so it seems that no מומחה is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But this implies…'. It introduces an inference from what a source did not say.
An expert declared it permitted, by confirming that the blemish is a valid, permanent one

phrases.english: But this implies a blemished one is permitted,
phrases.notes: An inference from the ברייתא, which forbade only a תם.

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא הִתִּירוּ מוּמְחֶה!
phrases.english: even though an expert did not permit it!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא בַּעַל מוּם שְׁרֵי, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא הִתִּירוּ מוּמְחֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues earlier, attacking the requirement of הִתִּירוֹ מוּמְחֶה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The earlier opinion (connected to רבי אסי / ריש לקיש) that the wool is permitted only once a מומחה has permitted the animal.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא forbids only a תם. By implication, any בעל מום is permitted, and no expert is mentioned.

steps.title: Answer: before an expert permits it, the animal still counts as unblemished
steps.stepSummary: The תנא of the ברייתא uses the word 'תם' for any animal that a מומחה has not yet permitted, even if it is physically blemished.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תנא calls any animal that an expert did not permit 'unblemished'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the expert requirement. It explains that the ברייתא's word 'תם' also covers a blemished animal that no expert has permitted yet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed that 'תם' means only physically unblemished. The answer gives 'תם' a legal meaning instead: not yet permitted by a מומחה. So the inference only permits a blemished animal that an expert did permit, which matches the earlier view.

keyTerms.meaning: Unblemished. Here it means legally unblemished: not yet permitted by an expert.

phrases.aramaic: תַּנָּא: כֹּל הֵיכָא דְּלֹא הִתִּירוֹ מוּמְחֶה —
phrases.english: The tanna: anywhere that an expert did not permit it —
he calls it 'unblemished'.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנָּא: כֹּל הֵיכָא דְּלֹא הִתִּירוֹ מוּמְחֶה — תָּם קָרֵי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 1 by redefining a word.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining a term (תם = not yet permitted by an expert).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'תם' means physically unblemished, so any blemished animal's wool would be permitted.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'תם' includes a blemished animal that no מומחה has permitted, so the expert requirement stands.
steps.confusionAlert: Here 'תם' does not mean 'has no blemish'. It means 'has not yet been officially permitted by an expert', even if a blemish is visible.

steps.title: Proposal of a dispute between תנאים, and the first case: wool plucked from an unblemished firstborn
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the expert requirement is debated by תנאים and begins quoting a ברייתא. Wool plucked while the בכור was תם stays forbidden, even if the animal later becomes blemished and is slaughtered.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say this is a dispute between תנאים: One who plucks wool from an unblemished firstborn — even though it later developed a blemish and he slaughtered it — the wool is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new move. It proposes that the expert requirement is really a dispute between תנאים, and starts quoting the ברייתא it will analyze.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This first case is undisputed. The status of the wool is fixed by the moment it was plucked. Because the animal was holy and unblemished then, the wool stays forbidden even after a later blemish and שחיטה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Let us say it is like (a dispute of) תנאים'. It proposes that a later view matches a tannaitic debate.
A firstborn animal, which is holy

phrases.english: Let us say it is like a dispute of tanna'im:
one who plucks wool from an unblemished firstborn,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁנּוֹלַד בּוֹ מוּם
phrases.english: even though a blemish later developed in it
and he slaughtered it — it is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending the expert requirement, the גמרא looks for a tannaitic dispute about it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wool plucked while the בכור was תם remains forbidden, even after a later blemish and שחיטה.

steps.title: עקביא בן מהללאל and the חכמים argue about a blemished firstborn that died
steps.stepSummary: Wool was plucked from a בכור בעל מום, and the animal then died without שחיטה. עקביא בן מהללאל permits the wool; the חכמים forbid it.
steps.simpleTranslation: A blemished firstborn from which one plucked wool, and afterward it died — עקביא בן מהללאל permits, and the חכמים forbid.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with a disputed case. The wool was plucked after the blemish appeared, but the animal died instead of being slaughtered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wool from a בעל מום could become permitted through proper שחיטה. If the animal dies, there is no שחיטה. The חכמים therefore forbid the wool, while עקביא permits it.

phrases.english: a blemished firstborn from which one plucked,
and afterward it died —
Akavya ben Mahalalel permits,
and the Rabbis forbid.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּכוֹר בַּעַל מוּם שֶׁתָּלַשׁ מִמֶּנּוּ, וְאַחַר כָּךְ מֵת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues quoting the same ברייתא. This is the opinion of the תנא קמא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Blemished בכור that died after its wool was plucked: עקביא permits the wool; the חכמים forbid it.

steps.title: רבי יהודה moves the dispute to hair that was shed before שחיטה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says עקביא did not permit in that case. The real dispute is about hair that fell off a blemished בכור and was stored in a niche, after which the animal was slaughtered.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה said: עקביא did not permit in this case. Rather, it was about hair of a blemished firstborn that fell out, and he put it in a niche, and afterward slaughtered the animal. In that case עקביא permits and the חכמים forbid.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה disagrees with the previous version of the dispute. He moves the argument to a different case: shed hair, followed by שחיטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יהודה, the argument is not about an animal that died. It is about hair that fell off on its own before the animal was slaughtered. עקביא says the later שחיטה permits the stored hair; the חכמים say it does not.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who offers a different version of the dispute
That fell out on its own
A wall niche or storage compartment (not a window here)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא בָּזֶה הִתִּיר עֲקַבְיָא בֶּן מַהֲלַלְאֵל,
phrases.english: not in this case did Akavya ben Mahalalel permit,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא בִּשְׂעַר בְּכוֹר בַּעַל מוּם שֶׁנָּשַׁר
phrases.english: rather, regarding hair of a blemished firstborn that fell out
and he placed it in a niche, and afterward slaughtered it —
in this case Akavya ben Mahalalel permits,
and the Rabbis forbid.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: לֹא בָּזֶה הִתִּיר עֲקַבְיָא בֶּן מַהֲלַלְאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disputes how the תנא קמא described עקביא's ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dispute is about shed hair of a בעל מום, followed by שחיטה. עקביא permits; the חכמים forbid.
steps.confusionAlert: Here 'חלון' means a storage niche or compartment in the wall, not a window.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: everyone agrees after שחיטה; the dispute is only when the animal died
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי reports that his father, חלפתא, agreed that slaughtered wool is permitted. The חכמים even said to store the shed hair in case the animal is later slaughtered. The dispute applies only when the animal died.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי said: My father חלפתא agrees in this case that it is permitted. Indeed, the חכמים explicitly said: put it in a niche, because perhaps there is hope. If he slaughtered it, everyone agrees it is permitted. If it died, עקביא permits and the חכמים forbid.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי gives a third description of the dispute. If the animal was slaughtered, everyone permits the wool; the argument is only about an animal that died.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים told people to store the shed hair because of the 'hope' that a later שחיטה will permit it. That instruction shows they agree that slaughtered wool is permitted. So רבי יהודה's case is not disputed, and the argument returns to the case of an animal that died.

keyTerms.meaning: Hope, a chance that it will become permitted

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei said:

phrases.aramaic: מוֹדֶה אַבָּא חֲלַפְתָּא בְּזֶה שֶׁהוּא מוּתָּר,
phrases.english: my father Ḥalafta agrees in this case that it is permitted,
indeed, the Rabbis said explicitly:
let him place it in a niche, since perhaps there is hope.
if he slaughtered it — all agree it is permitted,
if it died — Akavya ben Mahalalel permits
and the Rabbis forbid.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: מוֹדֶה אַבָּא חֲלַפְתָּא בְּזֶה שֶׁהוּא מוּתָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי יהודה's version and places the dispute back on an animal that died.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the animal was slaughtered, all permit the wool. If it died, עקביא permits and the חכמים forbid.
steps.confusionAlert: 'אבל' here does not mean 'but'. It means 'indeed', and it supports the previous statement.

steps.title: Challenge: רבי יוסי seems to say the same as the תנא קמא
steps.stepSummary: Both the תנא קמא and רבי יוסי put the dispute on a blemished animal that died. So what does רבי יוסי add?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי — that is the same as the first תנא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that רבי יוסי's view looks identical to the תנא קמא's. That should not be possible if they are disagreeing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא (step 4) said the dispute is about a blemished בכור that died. רבי יוסי says the same thing. Two opinions in a ברייתא should differ in some way, so a hidden difference must exist.

keyTerms.meaning: 'That is the same as'. It challenges an opinion as adding nothing new.
The first (anonymous) opinion in the ברייתא

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei — that is the same as the first tanna!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes the ברייתא just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The apparent difference between רבי יוסי and the תנא קמא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both put the dispute on an animal that died, so there seems to be no difference between them.

steps.title: Proposal: they differ about whether an expert permitted the animal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the difference between the תנא קמא and רבי יוסי is the requirement of הִתִּירוֹ מוּמְחֶה. That would make the expert requirement a dispute between תנאים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, is it not that they differ about whether an expert permitted it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by proposing a hidden difference: whether a מומחה permitted the animal. This also supports the opening suggestion of 'לימא כתנאי'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If both opinions sound the same on the surface, they must disagree about some unstated condition. The גמרא proposes that the condition is the expert's permission. That would show that the earlier view requiring an expert is debated by תנאים.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Rather, is it not…?' It introduces a suggested conclusion.

phrases.english: Rather, is it not whether an expert permitted it
that is between them?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לָאו הִתִּירוֹ מוּמְחֶה אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the קשיא of step 7 and supports the 'לימא כתנאי' suggestion of step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifying a hidden practical difference (נפקא מינה)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוסי simply repeats the תנא קמא.
steps.terutzMaskana: They differ about whether הִתִּירוֹ מוּמְחֶה is required, so the expert requirement is a dispute between תנאים.
steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא tries to show that the requirement that a מומחה permit the blemish is itself debated by תנאים. It does this by finding a hidden difference between רבי יוסי and the תנא קמא.
steps.whyThisMatters: If the expert requirement is a dispute between תנאים, then the earlier view is not universally accepted. The next part of the sugya will test whether this suggestion holds.

steps.title: Spelling out the expert-permission difference
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains its suggestion. The תנא קמא permits the wool only if an expert permitted the animal before the wool fell. רבי יוסי permits it even without an expert.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תנא קמא holds: if an expert permitted it, yes; if not, no. רבי יוסי comes to say: even if an expert did not permit it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the answer it started in Step 8. It shows exactly how the תנא קמא and רבי יוסי would differ over the expert requirement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא's case is read as one where an expert had already declared the blemish before the wool fell. That is why the wool can be permitted. רבי יוסי adds that it is permitted even without such an expert, so the rule of הִתִּירוֹ מוּמְחֶה becomes a dispute between תנאים.

keyTerms.meaning: The first, unnamed teacher of the ברייתא
An expert permitted it, i.e., examined the blemish and allowed slaughter

phrases.english: For the first tanna holds:
if an expert permitted it, then yes (the wool is permitted),
and if not, then no,
and Rabbi Yosei comes to say:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּלֹא הִתִּירוֹ מוּמְחֶה!
phrases.english: even though an expert did not permit it!

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנָּא קַמָּא סָבַר הִתִּירוֹ מוּמְחֶה אִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer suggested in Step 8
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifying a hidden point of dispute between תנאים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוסי seems to just repeat the תנא קמא
steps.terutzMaskana: They differ over whether הִתִּירוֹ מוּמְחֶה is required

steps.title: רבא: everyone requires an expert
steps.stepSummary: רבא rejects the suggestion. All agree that the wool is permitted only if an expert permitted the animal beforehand.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: No. Everyone agrees that if an expert permitted it, yes; if he did not permit it, no.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pushes back on the answer from Steps 8–9. He says the expert rule is not in dispute at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By making the expert requirement agreed upon by all, רבא removes it as the difference between the תנא קמא and רבי יוסי. This means he must find another difference, which he gives next.

keyTerms.meaning: רבא, the אמורא who rejects the suggestion

phrases.english: Rava said: No,

phrases.aramaic: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא אִי הִתִּירוֹ מוּמְחֶה — אִין,
phrases.english: for everyone agrees: if an expert permitted it, yes,
if he did not permit it, no,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the expert-based explanation of Steps 8–9
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that הִתִּירוֹ מוּמְחֶה is a dispute between תנאים
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: All תנאים require an expert, so this cannot be what separates them

steps.title: Three disputes: the first view says they argue in both cases
steps.stepSummary: רבא says there are three opinions on where the dispute lies. The תנא קמא holds that עקביא and the חכמים argue both when the animal died and when it was slaughtered. He mentions 'died' only to show how far עקביא goes.
steps.simpleTranslation: There are three disputes in this matter. The תנא קמא holds they argue about a dead animal, and the same is true about a slaughtered one. He says they argue about a dead animal only to show you the strength of עקביא's position.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא now gives his own answer to the question of Step 7. He begins with the תנא קמא's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the תנא קמא, the חכמים forbid the wool even if the animal was slaughtered. He chose to describe the 'died' case to show that עקביא permits even there. So the תנא קמא disagrees with רבי יוסי, who says that in a slaughtered case everyone permits.

keyTerms.meaning: Three disputes, meaning three opinions on where the argument lies
To show you the strength (far reach) of his position

steps.confusionAlert: 'Three disputes' does not mean three separate laws. It means three תנאים disagree about which case עקביא and the חכמים actually argue about.

phrases.english: And there are three disputes in this matter,
for the first tanna holds: they disagree about one that died,
and the same is true about one he slaughtered,
and the reason it says they disagree about one that died
is to show you the strength of Akavya's position.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבא's replacement answer after rejecting the expert explanation
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the scope of the dispute
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The תנא קמא and רבי יוסי both seem to place the dispute only on a dead animal
steps.terutzMaskana: The תנא קמא holds they argue in both cases. 'Died' is mentioned only to show עקביא's strength.

steps.title: The second and third views: רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה holds that everyone forbids the wool of a dead animal, and they argue only about a slaughtered one. רבי יוסי holds that everyone permits the wool of a slaughtered animal, and they argue only about a dead one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה holds: about a dead animal, all agree it is forbidden; they argue about a slaughtered one. רבי יוסי comes to say: about a slaughtered one, all agree it is permitted; they argue about a dead one.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא finishes his list by giving the other two opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The three views are mirror images. The תנא קמא says the dispute covers both cases. רבי יהודה says it covers only the slaughtered case. רבי יוסי says it covers only the dead case. This answers Step 7: רבי יוסי does add something, because he says a slaughtered animal's wool is permitted by everyone.
steps.whatToRemember: The three opinions, by where the dispute lies: the תנא קמא says both cases; רבי יהודה says slaughtered only (dead is forbidden by all); רבי יוסי says dead only (slaughtered is permitted by all).

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda holds:
about one that died, all agree it is forbidden,
when they disagree, it is about one he slaughtered,
and Rabbi Yosei comes to say:
about one he slaughtered, all agree it is permitted,
when they disagree, it is about one that died.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה סָבַר בְּמֵת דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל אָסוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבא's three-way list begun in Step 11
steps.terutzResolutionType: Mapping the scope of the dispute for each תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוסי adds nothing beyond the תנא קמא
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוסי adds that a slaughtered animal's wool is permitted by everyone

steps.title: רב נחמן rules like רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן rules that the הלכה follows רבי יהודה, because the משנה in בחירתא (עדיות) matches his view.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: The הלכה follows רבי יהודה, since we learned a משנה in בחירתא that agrees with him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן gives the practical ruling and says he has a source. The source itself comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מסכת עדיות is called בחירתא, 'the chosen one,' because its rulings were set on a special day in the בית מדרש. A משנה there carries extra weight, so it decides between the three views.

keyTerms.meaning: רב נחמן, the אמורא who decides the הלכה
'The chosen one,' a name for מסכת עדיות

steps.whyThisMatters: This gives the practical outcome. The wool of a dead בכור is forbidden by all, and the argument is only over a slaughtered one.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said:
The halakha follows Rabbi Yehuda,
since we learned in the 'chosen' tractate (Eduyot) in accordance with him,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides among the three views listed by רבא
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows רבי יהודה. The dispute between עקביא and the חכמים is only about a slaughtered animal.

steps.title: The משנה in עדיות that matches רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה in עדיות sets the dispute between עקביא and the חכמים in a case where the shed hair was stored and the animal was then slaughtered. That is exactly רבי יהודה's version.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: the hair of a blemished בכור that fell out, and he put it in a niche, and afterward he slaughtered the animal. עקביא בן מהללאל permits, and the חכמים forbid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the source behind רב נחמן's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה places the argument in the slaughtered case, using the same words as רבי יהודה in Step 5. רבי יוסי says everyone permits when the animal was slaughtered, so the משנה rules out his version and matches רבי יהודה's.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה
A wall niche or storage compartment (not a window here)

phrases.english: As we learned:
the hair of a blemished firstborn that fell out,
and he placed it in a niche,
and afterward he slaughtered it:
Akavya ben Mahalalel permits,
and the Rabbis forbid.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן שְׂעַר בְּכוֹר בַּעַל מוּם שֶׁנָּשַׁר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the משנה source for רב נחמן's ruling
steps.raayaObject: רב נחמן's ruling that the הלכה follows רבי יהודה
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה עדיות ה:ו, which places the dispute in the slaughtered case

steps.title: Our משנה also supports רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק says our משנה also supports רבי יהודה, and quotes the rule about loose wool hanging from a בכור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: Our משנה is also precise and shows this, as we learned: wool that is dangling from a firstborn animal, the part that looks like it belongs with the fleece is permitted, and the part that does not look like it belongs with the fleece is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק brings a second proof that the הלכה follows רבי יהודה, this time from our own משנה. He quotes the rule about wool that is partly loose and still hanging from a בכור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 14 brought support from the משנה in עדיות. Now a new source is added: a careful reading of our משנה's clause about dangling wool. The proof is not spelled out yet, and the next steps will show why only רבי יהודה fits this rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה is also precise, meaning a careful reading of it proves the point
Dangling wool: wool that has come partly loose but still hangs on the animal
A firstborn animal, which is holy, so its wool may not be used
The fleece, meaning the wool that is sheared off

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:
Our Mishnah is also precise and shows this,
phrases.notes: The point it shows is that the הלכה follows רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: as we learned: wool dangling from a firstborn animal,
the part that looks like it belongs with the fleece is permitted,
and the part that does not look like it belongs with the fleece is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second proof for רב נחמן's ruling in step 13, alongside the עדיות proof in step 14.
steps.raayaObject: That the הלכה follows רבי יהודה's version of the dispute between עקביא and the חכמים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The dangling-wool clause of our משנה.

steps.title: Whose view is this rule? Testing רבי יוסי first
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whose view the dangling-wool rule follows, and first tests רבי יוסי by asking which case he would be talking about.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? If you say it is רבי יוסי, then in what case is it talking about?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts working out the proof. It asks whose opinion the dangling-wool rule follows, and begins by trying רבי יוסי. This is a setup line for the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof works by ruling out options one by one. For each version of the dispute, the גמרא asks which case the rule could be about: an animal that was slaughtered or one that died.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say, which introduces an option that will be tested

phrases.english: Whose view is this?
If you say it is Rabbi Yosei, then in what case?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins explaining how the משנה quoted in step 15 proves the point.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which version of the dispute, and which case, the dangling-wool rule fits.

steps.title: Under רבי יוסי, a slaughtered animal does not fit
steps.stepSummary: If the rule follows רבי יוסי and the animal was slaughtered, everyone would permit all the wool, so the משנה's split between the two kinds of wool makes no sense.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it is about a case where he slaughtered the animal, then whether you follow עקביא or the רבנן, both kinds of wool are permitted!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the idea that the rule follows רבי יוסי in the case of a slaughtered animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי holds that everyone permits the wool of a slaughtered animal (step 12). If so, there is no reason to forbid wool that does not look like part of the fleece. Since the משנה does forbid it, this case cannot be what the משנה means.

keyTerms.meaning: This one and that one, meaning both kinds of wool

phrases.english: If you say it is where he slaughtered it,
whether according to Akavya or according to the Rabbis,
both this wool and that wool are permitted!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the first case under רבי יוסי and rules it out.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The option that the rule follows רבי יוסי in the case of a slaughtered animal.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: According to רבי יוסי, no one forbids wool from a slaughtered animal, so the משנה would have no reason to forbid any of it.

steps.title: Under רבי יוסי, a dead animal does not fit either
steps.stepSummary: If the animal died, the רבנן would forbid both kinds of wool. עקביא would rule the opposite of the משנה: wool that looks attached is forbidden, and wool that looks loose is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, is it about an animal that died? If it follows the רבנן, both kinds of wool are forbidden. If it follows עקביא, the opposite should be true: wool that looks like part of the fleece is forbidden, because the death forbids it, and wool that does not look like part of the fleece is permitted, because it was already detached from the start!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the other case under רבי יוסי, an animal that died, and shows that this does not match the משנה either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יוסי, the dispute is about a dead animal. The רבנן forbid even wool that came off fully, so they would surely forbid dangling wool too. עקביא would treat wool that looks attached as still part of the animal, so the death forbids it. He would treat wool that looks loose as already detached, so it is permitted. That is exactly the reverse of the משנה, so רבי יוסי is out.

keyTerms.meaning: The animal died on its own, without שחיטה
He should have said the opposite
Detached, already plucked off the animal

steps.confusionAlert: Under עקביא, looking attached makes the wool forbidden, not permitted. Wool that looks attached counts as part of the animal, so it is forbidden when the animal dies. That is why עקביא's view would flip the משנה.

phrases.english: Rather, is it about an animal that died?

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי רַבָּנַן — אִידֵּי וְאִידֵּי מֵיסָר אָסְרִי,
phrases.english: If it follows the Rabbis, both this and that are forbidden,
and if it follows Akavya, it should have said the opposite:
wool that looks like part of the fleece is forbidden,
because the death forbids it;
phrases.notes: It counts as still attached to the animal when it died.

phrases.english: wool that does not look like part of the fleece is permitted,
because it was detached from the start!
phrases.notes: It came loose before the animal died.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rules out the remaining case under רבי יוסי, which closes the רבי יוסי option.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The option that the rule follows רבי יוסי in the case of a dead animal, under either side of the dispute.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The רבנן would forbid both kinds of wool, and עקביא would rule the reverse of the משנה.

steps.title: So the rule must follow רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: Since רבי יוסי does not fit, the גמרא concludes that the rule must follow רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is obvious that it follows רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: Having ruled out רבי יוסי, the גמרא turns to רבי יהודה as the only remaining option. This line prepares the test of which case רבי יהודה would be talking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the גמרא needs to show that the משנה makes sense according to רבי יהודה. The next step checks which case, dead or slaughtered, fits his view.

phrases.english: Rather, it is obvious that it follows Rabbi Yehuda,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Switches to the remaining option after both cases under רבי יוסי failed.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rule could have followed רבי יוסי.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only רבי יהודה remains as a possible author of the rule.

steps.title: Under רבי יהודה, a dead animal does not fit
steps.stepSummary: Under רבי יהודה, if the animal died, both עקביא and the רבנן forbid all the wool. So the משנה's split cannot be about a dead animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: And in what case? If you say it is about an animal that died, then according to both עקביא and the רבנן, both kinds of wool are forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rules out the dead-animal case under רבי יהודה. This sets up the next move: the rule must be about a slaughtered animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה holds that everyone forbids the wool of a dead animal (step 12). So in that case no wool could be permitted, but the משנה permits wool that looks like part of the fleece. Only the slaughtered case is left, and the גמרא will explain it next.

keyTerms.meaning: Whether according to עקביא or according to the רבנן

phrases.english: And in what case? If you say an animal that died,
whether according to Akavya or according to the Rabbis,
both this wool and that wool are forbidden!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the first case under רבי יהודה and rules it out. The slaughtered case remains for the next step.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The option that the rule follows רבי יהודה in the case of a dead animal.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: According to רבי יהודה, everyone forbids wool from a dead animal, so the משנה could not permit any of it.

steps.title: In a slaughtered animal, the rule cannot follow עקביא
steps.stepSummary: Since a dead animal did not work, the משנה must be about a slaughtered animal. But עקביא would permit all the wool there, so the rule cannot follow him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, isn't the משנה talking about a case where he slaughtered the animal? But if it follows עקביא, he permits both kinds of wool!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the only case left, a slaughtered animal. It shows that עקביא cannot be the author of the משנה even there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 20 ruled out a dead animal. So the משנה must be about a slaughtered one. In a slaughtered animal, עקביא permits all the wool, whether or not it looks attached to the fleece. That leaves no room for the משנה's split between the two kinds of wool.

keyTerms.meaning: when he slaughtered it (as opposed to the animal dying on its own)
עקביא בן מהללאל, the תנא who disagrees with the רבנן about wool from a בכור

phrases.english: Rather, is it not where he slaughtered it?
phrases.notes: The only option left after the dead-animal case failed.

phrases.english: And if it is Akavya,
both this and that he fully permits!
phrases.notes: Both the wool that looks attached and the wool that does not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the rejected dead-animal case to the slaughtered-animal case, and eliminates עקביא there.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rules out עקביא as the author of the משנה in a slaughtered animal.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: עקביא permits all the wool of a slaughtered animal, so he could not make the משנה's split.

steps.title: The rule follows the רבנן, and the dispute is about a slaughtered animal
steps.stepSummary: The משנה must follow the רבנן. This proves that עקביא and the רבנן disagree in a slaughtered animal. The גמרא confirms this.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, isn't it the רבנן? And learn from this that they argue about a slaughtered animal. Yes, learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: Only the רבנן are left as the author of the משנה. From this the גמרא draws a new fact about the dispute, and then confirms it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה splits the wool into two kinds, and only the רבנן split it that way in a slaughtered animal. So the משנה follows the רבנן, within רבי יהודה's version of the dispute. This proves that עקביא and the רבנן argue about a slaughtered animal, which רבי יוסי denied, since he says everyone permits after שחיטה. This completes רב נחמן בר יצחק's support for רב נחמן's ruling like רבי יהודה (Step 13).

keyTerms.meaning: the Sages, the majority view opposing עקביא
learn from this; when repeated at the end, it means 'yes, that is correct'

steps.whatToRemember: The dangling-wool משנה follows the רבנן within רבי יהודה's version. This shows that עקביא and the רבנן argue about a slaughtered animal, against רבי יוסי. That supports רב נחמן's ruling that the הלכה follows רבי יהודה.
steps.confusionAlert: The phrase שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ appears twice. The first time, it is part of a question: 'should we learn from this?' The second time, standing alone, it is the answer: 'yes, learn from it.'

phrases.english: Rather, is it not the Rabbis?
And learn from it: they disagree where he slaughtered it.
Indeed, learn from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לָאו רַבָּנַן הִיא? וּשְׁמַע מִינַּהּ: בִּשְׁחָטוֹ פְּלִיגִי. שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Once עקביא is eliminated, the only author left is the רבנן, and the conclusion follows from that.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה follows the רבנן, and עקביא and the רבנן disagree about a slaughtered animal. This confirms רבי יהודה's version and רב נחמן's ruling.

steps.title: רבי ינאי asks about wool from a perfect עולה
steps.stepSummary: רבי ינאי asks what the law is when someone pulls wool off an unblemished עולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ינאי asked: if someone pulls wool off a perfect עולה, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic starts. רבי ינאי asks a question about wool from a perfect, unblemished עולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the discussion was about a בכור. Now the question moves to an עולה. As worded, the question talks about someone who actively pulls the wool out. The next step will challenge that wording.

keyTerms.meaning: one who plucks or pulls out

phrases.english: Rabbi Yannai raised a dilemma:
one who plucks wool from an unblemished burnt offering, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic after the previous discussion was concluded.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether wool taken from an unblemished עולה is permitted or forbidden.

steps.title: Pulling wool on purpose is obviously forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: if someone pulls the wool out on purpose, nobody would permit it, so what is the question?
steps.simpleTranslation: Pulling it out? Is there anyone who permits that?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording of רבי ינאי's question. Pulling wool from a holy animal is clearly forbidden, so there is nothing to ask.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pulling wool off a holy animal is an act of shearing it, which is not allowed. Everyone agrees such wool is forbidden. So the question as worded has no real doubt in it.

keyTerms.meaning: is there anyone who permits? (meaning: certainly not)

phrases.english: Plucks? Is there anyone who permits it?
phrases.notes: A rhetorical question. Everyone forbids wool pulled out on purpose.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the wording of רבי ינאי's question.
steps.kashyaTarget: The word הַתּוֹלֵשׁ in רבי ינאי's question.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Wool pulled out on purpose is forbidden by everyone, so there is no doubt to ask about.

steps.title: The real question is about wool that fell out by itself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rewords the question: what about wool that came loose on its own from a perfect עולה?
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he meant: wool that came out by itself from a perfect עולה, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the wording of רבי ינאי's question. He was asking about wool that fell out on its own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word changes from הַתּוֹלֵשׁ, 'one who pulls', to שֶׁנִּתְלַשׁ, 'that came out by itself'. Nobody did anything forbidden here. So it is a real question whether the wool is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: that was torn out (by itself, without anyone pulling it)

phrases.english: Rather, wool that was torn out by itself
from an unblemished burnt offering, what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, צֶמֶר שֶׁנִּתְלַשׁ מֵעוֹלָה תְּמִימָה, מַהוּ?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection by rewording the question.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The question was about someone who pulls the wool out on purpose.
steps.terutzMaskana: The question is about wool that fell out on its own.

steps.title: No question about a חטאת or an אשם
steps.stepSummary: For a חטאת or an אשם there is no doubt. These offerings bring atonement, so the owner will not delay bringing them.
steps.simpleTranslation: About a חטאת and an אשם you need not ask. Since they come for atonement, people do not keep them waiting.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts narrowing down where the real doubt is. First it removes the חטאת and the אשם from the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Forbidding loose wool would be a protective rule. It would stop an owner from keeping the animal around for its wool, which could lead him to shear it. A person who needs atonement brings his חטאת or אשם quickly. So there is no need for that protection, and the wool is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: you need not ask (the answer is clear)
they keep it waiting, delay it

phrases.english: Concerning a sin offering and a guilt offering, do not ask,
since they come for atonement,
people do not keep them waiting.
phrases.notes: So there is no reason to forbid the wool.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the question by removing the clear cases.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wool that falls from a חטאת or an אשם is not forbidden, because the owner will not delay these offerings.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the reasoning behind the whole question: wool is forbidden only where there is a fear that the owner will delay bringing the offering.

steps.title: No question about a בכור or a מעשר either
steps.stepSummary: For a בכור and a מעשר the answer is also clear. They do not bring atonement, so the owner might keep them waiting, and the wool is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: About a בכור and a מעשר you also need not ask. Since they do not come for atonement, people may keep them waiting.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא removes the second clear case, the opposite of the first one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בכור and a מעשר do not bring atonement, so the owner has no pressure to bring them quickly. He might keep the animal around and come to shear it or use it for work. That is why the loose wool is forbidden here.

phrases.english: Concerning a firstborn and a tithe animal also, do not ask,
since they do not come for atonement,
people keep them waiting.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The opposite case of step 26, showing the other clear outcome.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wool that falls from a בכור or a מעשר is forbidden, because the owner may delay bringing them.

steps.title: The real doubt is about an עולה
steps.stepSummary: The real question is about an עולה. The reasoning begins with the word 'since', and this passage ends there.
steps.simpleTranslation: When you ask, it is about an עולה. What is the law? Since…
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names the case that is really in doubt, the עולה. It begins to explain why, and the explanation continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עולה sits between the two clear cases. In some ways it is like a חטאת, and in some ways it is like a בכור. So it is not clear whether the owner will delay bringing it. The word כֵּיוָן opens the first side of the argument.

keyTerms.meaning: where you should ask (the real question)

steps.confusionAlert: The text stops in the middle of a sentence. Do not try to answer the question yet. The two sides of the doubt are explained in the next lines.

phrases.english: Where you should ask is about a burnt offering. What is the law?
Since…
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי תִּיבְּעֵי לָךְ דְּעוֹלָה, מַאי? כֵּיוָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After removing the two clear cases, the גמרא focuses on the one case that is in doubt.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether an עולה is treated like the atonement offerings, so its wool is permitted, or like the non-atonement animals, so its wool is forbidden.
